Criterion: Verify that engine fire zone (nacelle/cowling) cooling and ventilation provisions are adequate to provide required heat rejection and maintain engine fire zone conditions necessary to avoid both hot surface ignition sources and collection of vapors. Standard: Engine bays/nacelles are ventilated with the greater of: a. Between 2-3 volumetric air changes per minute. b. The minimum required flow to keep hot surfaces less than autoignition temperature of the fuel or other flammable fluid in or near the engine bay. Method of Compliance: Design analysis and thermal models establish heat rejection and cooling requirements for components for normal and worst case operations and environments. Component tests verify heat rejection models. Ground and flight tests verify cooling capability to eliminate the presence of hot surface ignition during all expected flight and ground conditions. Installed ground and flight tests verify ventilation capability to remove hazardous fluids and vapors to a safe location during all expected flight and ground conditions. References: JSSG-2009: G.3.4.7.4, G.4.4.7.4, G.3.4.7.18, G.4.4.7.18 14 CFR 23.851-23.865, 25.851-25.869, 23.1181-23.1203, 25.1181-25.1207, 23.1411, 25.1411, 27.863, 27.865, 29.851, 29.863, 29.865, 27.1411, 29.1411

Standard: Sufficient cooling air mass flow through fire zones is provided to ensure that the temperature limits for all items within, including engines or APUs, accessory equipment, the supporting structure, and the compartment itself within the zone, are not exceeded under any operating condition. Surface temperatures are maintained below the hot surface ignition temperature of any flammable fluids present, and compartment air temperature is maintained below the auto-ignition temperature for any flammable vapors present. Method of Compliance: Prior to entering flight test, verify the standard by the following method(s): Analysis.
(1) Conduct design analysis and thermal model analysis to show the heat rejection and cooling needed to prevent hot surface and auto-ignition sources are provided under all flight and ground operating conditions. Test.
  (1) Lab test: Conduct lab tests to verify thermal analysis of predicted surface temperatures of components.
  (2) Ground test: Conduct ground tests to validate analysis that shows the heat rejection and cooling needed to prevent hot surface and auto-ignition sources is provided under all flight and ground operating conditions. Prior to entering operational test/operations, verify the standard by the above and following method(s): Test.
  (3) Flight test: Conduct flight tests to validate analysis that shows the heat rejection and cooling needed to prevent hot surface and auto-ignition sources is provided under all flight and ground operating conditions.
